messages:
lena: Quick summary from the nsys sparse-sampling experiment I ran on staging this morning. Wanted to share raw numbers and get opinions on safe production sampling params.
marc: awesome, thanks. quick TL;DR first?
lena: TL;DR: sparse sampling (1/200 full nsys captures + 1/50 lightweight kernel timeline sampling) added ~0.7% p99 latency and ~1.2% CPU overhead on the host. NV kernel time attribution changed for very short kernels (<=40us) when nsys attached.
gabe: can you paste the commands you ran?
lena: sure — full capture used for ground truth:```nsys profile -o out_full -t cuda,nvtx --sample=none --capture-range=kernel --force-overwrite --trace-fork-before-exec true -- python run_microbench.py --batch-size=1```sparse sampling controller:```# controller (pseudo) every 200 reqs -> spawn full nsys capture for that reqs' GPU task every 50 reqs -> collect kernel timeline via lightweight tracer (nsys --sample frequency reduced)```
anya: when you say "lightweight tracer" what flags?
lena: lightweight:```nsys profile -o out_light -t cuda --sampling-interval=10ms --capture-range=none --trace-fork-before-exec false --duration=200ms```that produced a timeline with much lower overhead but loses short kernel resolution.
marc: numbers? overhead breakdown?
lena: raw experiment (avg over 5 runs, 8-GPU pool, mixed seq lengths):
- baseline (no profiler): median latency 12.1ms, p99 45.2ms, host CPU 18%
- full nsys every req (for experiment only): median 12.9ms, p99 78.4ms, host CPU 34%
- sparse (1/200 full + 1/50 light): median 12.2ms, p99 46.1ms, host CPU 19.4%
- lightweight-only (1/50 light): median 12.15ms, p99 46.0ms, host CPU 19.1%
notes: the big p99 jump only happens if you profile *that* request with full nsys. sparse keeps p99 close to baseline.
gabe: interesting. did you see kernel selection flip-flops because of profiler timing noise?
lena: yes — for kernels <40us we saw kernel selection change due to altered launch timings; the runtime picked a different kernel (small-workload fallback) ~12% of the time when full nsys attached. For larger kernels (>300us) behavior stable.
anya: that's concerning for safe-prod. any mitigation ideas?
marc: configurable guardrail: never run full nsys on requests that hit the "fast-path" kernels (we can detect by checking request profile and skip). Also prefer event-based sampling triggered by anomaly (e.g., latency spike) instead of uniform sampling.
lena: experiments on adaptive sampling: if request latency > 1.5x running median -> trigger full capture (rate-limited to 1/hour per node). That captured real regressions with acceptable cost in my runbook.
gabe: how about KV cache & batching interplay? does sampling bias KV hit rates?
lena: short answer: yes. When nsys attaches, microsecond jitter sometimes prevents KV cache de-dup window from coalescing, increasing observed cache misses by ~0.8 percentage points in the full-capture runs. Sparse sampling reduces this distortion because the vast majority of requests are uninstrumented.
anya: do we have a suggested safe config to try on canary clusters?
marc: proposed safe defaults:```- lightweight-sample: 1/100 requests (nsys sampling interval 20ms, duration 150ms) - full-trace: anomaly-triggered (latency > 2x median) OR scheduled 1/1000 requests - rate-limit full-trace: max 2 full traces per node per 24h - skip full-trace for requests that match fast-path signature (kernel durations < 50us) - KV/batching sanity check: if sampled run shows >1% delta in KV hit-rate vs baseline, mark trace as noisy and discard```
gabe: feels reasonable. we should also add an automatic rollback: if any full-trace increases p99 on the host by >5% across the node, abort further full-traces for 1 hour.
lena: +1. I also suggest attaching a short perfetto capture (user-space only) in parallel for full-traces to cross-reference without CUDA attach. perfetto user-space had effectively zero kernel perturbation in my tests.
anya: outstanding actions?
marc: - lena to push the sampling controller prototype and experiment logs to the repo. - gabe to add fast-path detector to the runtime (heuristic: median kernel <50us for the request). - anya to draft runbook with guardrails & rollback policy. schedule canary run for next Tue 09:00 UTC.
lena: I'll upload the raw csvs and a short notebook with plots (p99 delta, CPU overhead, KV-hit delta). link will be in the ticket.
profiling-bot: scheduled canary run created: canary-nsys-sparse-2026-03-24-09-00 (id: 42).
marc: great. if we keep full-trace rare and guarded, seems safe to get production-level signals without disrupting users. thanks all.
